writeup.headline: GEO rates Hold: solid growth and strong share momentum offset by heavy debt and thin free cash flow.
writeup.thesis: GEO scores 49, a Hold, sitting 5 points above the Sell line and 16 points short of Buy. Growth is decent, with TTM revenue growth of 15.3% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 15.1% year on year, though growth slowed by 1.6 pp from the previous quarter. The trend factor is the strongest at 74: shares are up 82.2% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago and are 36.4 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days, though the price is 10.1% below its 50-day average. The balance sheet scores just 2, with net debt at 55.09 times free cash flow and cash covering only 0.04 of debt, because the FCF margin is a thin 0.9% despite an 11.2% operating margin. Valuation scores 28: P/FCF of 137.3x is high in absolute terms, the FCF yield is 4.3 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, and the stock is expensive against its own history.
key_risks: Very high leverage relative to free cash flow (net debt to FCF of 55.09) and little cash against debt.
Heavy dependence on ICE, including rebid risk on the Aurora contract, now extended only to December 15.
The long-running forced-labor class action heading toward a jury trial.
Free cash flow is thin (0.9% margin), leaving the stock at 137.3x FCF and expensive against its own history.
Momentum is fading short term, with the price 10.1% below its 50-day average and 15.9% below its 52-week high.
what_would_change: A drop of 5 points would push the rating to Sell, for example if the trend factor weakens further or the November 5 Q3 results disappoint.
A sustained rise in free cash flow would help both the balance sheet and valuation scores, the main drags on the rating.
Winning the larger 10-year Aurora contract or new guidance raises could lift growth and news scores toward the 16 points needed for Buy.
An adverse outcome in the forced-labor litigation or a lost ICE contract would weigh on news risk and push toward Sell.
